confidence_notes: Holistic estimate from general knowledge; no live listings or menus were checked. Restaurant anchors are moderately reliable; accommodation is less certain given July seasonality. Cocktail and wine use the local price relationship to beer (about 2.5x and 1.5x beer) because direct knowledge is weaker. USD values assume an approximate working rate of R17.5 per USD, not a live quote. The fx value comes from search-result summaries attributed to the RBA listing; I did not open the page, and the 15 October date was flagged for confirmation.
comparable_city_reasoning: Regional basis: general South African urban-tourism price levels, with Cape Town placed toward the higher end of comparable South African tourist cities because of accommodation demand and restaurant and wine-region pricing; no external price source was consulted.

anchor_basis.beer: 340 ml draft Castle Lager at a Cape Town restaurant or bar, about R55
anchor_basis.coffee: regular cappuccino at a neighbourhood cafe, about R50
anchor_basis.inexp_meal_1p: chicken burger and chips at a casual local restaurant, about R130 before drinks
anchor_basis.midrange_meal_2p: starter, main and dessert for two at a mid-range bistro, about R1,000 total without drinks
anchor_basis.cocktail: standard gin and tonic or similar cocktail at a mid-range bar, about R140
anchor_basis.wine_glass: 175 ml glass of a mid-range South African wine at a restaurant, about R80
anchor_basis.hostel_dorm_1p: one bed in a six-bed mixed dorm at a registered Cape Town hostel, about R280 per night
anchor_basis.hostel_private_2p: private double room at a registered hostel, about R750 per night
